kind.title: Screen at eye level
kind.body: The top of the monitor sits at or just below your eyes, about an arm's length away.

kind.title: Supported back
kind.body: Sit back in the chair so it holds the curve of your lower back.

kind.title: Feet flat
kind.body: Both feet rest on the floor or a footrest, knees about level with your hips.

text.text: “Sitting up straight all day is best.”

slides.title: Lesson 2: Breathe
slides.notes: When the day speeds up, your breath is the quickest way to slow it down.

kind.text: When the day speeds up, your breath is the quickest way to slow it down.

slides.title: Breathe with the circle
slides.notes: Follow the circle. Breathe in as it grows, hold for a moment, and breathe out slowly as it shrinks.

kind.text: Watch the circle grow as you breathe in, rest as you hold, and shrink as you breathe out.

objects.name: Breathing circle
objects.description: A circle that grows and shrinks with your breath

slides.title: A one-minute reset

kind.text: Feet flat, hands resting in your lap. Let your shoulders drop away from your ears.

kind.alt: A woman breathing calmly

kind.text: Breathe in slowly through your nose while you count to four.

kind.alt: A woman breathing calmly

kind.text: Hold the breath gently, without strain, for another count of four.

kind.alt: A woman breathing calmly

kind.text: Let the air out through your mouth for a count of six. Repeat three times.

kind.alt: A woman breathing calmly

slides.title: Bonus: blink and the 20-20-20 rule
slides.notes: Blink more, and the 20-20-20 rule explained.

kind.alt: A man resting his eyes by looking out of a window

kind.text:
Blink more, and
look far away

Every 20 minutes
look 20 feet (6 m) away
for 20 seconds
At a screen we blink about half as often, which dries the eyes. A few slow blinks keep them comfortable.
Want more? Read the WHO physical activity fact sheet.

glossary.definition: Fitting the workspace to the person: chair, desk, screen and tools set up so your body stays comfortable.
A pause of one to five minutes to stand, stretch, look away or breathe.
Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet (about 6 metres) away for 20 seconds.
Breathing in, holding and breathing out to a steady count, such as 4-4-6, to calm the body.
A one-to-one or small catch-up held on foot, ideally outside, instead of at a screen.
